messages:
sara: Heads-up — after landing PTQ per-channel for reranker-v2 I'm seeing ~0.8% absolute MRR@10 drop on the long-tail split. Not huge but consistent across two runs. anyone else?

mike: oh interesting. did you run the same eval harness as before? dataset + tokenization exact?

sara: same dataset (webqa-longtail-v3 holdout), same prompt templates. I did notice tokenization differences when loading the new weights with tokenizer v3 vs v2 — some doc truncation shifted by 1-2 tokens. could that explain it? :thinking:

julian: tokenization shift can definitely change ranking when candidates are near cutoff. what's the seq_len and truncation side you used?

sara: seq_len=512, trunc_side=right, context concat = title + " - " + snippet. ran `python eval.py --model rerank-v2-ptq-perchannel --split holdout --batch 128 --metric mrr@10` locally.

oli: can you paste the exact eval cmd and a tiny sample input where it flips? sometimes whitespace normalization changes token boundaries.

sara: sure, example snippet below (sanitized):

```
QUERY: "install nginx on ubuntu 20.04"
DOC A: "Step 1: apt update\nStep 2: apt install nginx -y\n..."  (ranks 1 before PTQ)
DOC B: "Use apt-get install nginx ..." (ranks 2 before PTQ)
```

After PTQ per-channel, order flips for ~3% of queries in the long tail.

anika: do we have bootstrap CI runs for statistical significance? small deltas can be noise.

ci-bot: bootstrap job queued: eval/webqa-longtail-v3 | rerank-v2-ptq-perchannel vs rerank-v2-fp16 | bootstrap=5000 | metric=ndcg@10,mrr@10

ci-bot: bootstrap job finished: ndcg@10 diff = -0.006 (p=0.031), mrr@10 diff = -0.008 (p=0.018). 95% CI non-overlapping.

mike: ok p<0.05 on both metrics — worth investigating. did you compare per-length or per-query-position slices?

sara: sliced by query length and candidate doc length. signal concentrated on queries with >150 tokens docs that get truncated at 512. also stronger on queries that rely on title-only signals.

julian: that aligns with tokenizer shift + quantization interacting: per-channel PTQ changes calibration on low-activation heads -> different attention scaling for late tokens. per-layer PTQ behaves differently.

anika: can we reproduce by forcing tokenizer v2 + per-channel PTQ and then tokenizer v3 + per-channel PTQ to isolate tokenizer vs quantization?

oli: yes — run matrix: {tokenizer_v2, tokenizer_v3} x {fp16, ptq-perlayer, ptq-perchannel} x 3 seeds. collect ndcg@10, mrr@10 and bootstrap CI. I can help wire it into the CI harness.

ci-bot: note: our CI harness default max_seq=768 for fp16 but local evals used 512. mismatch flagged.

mike: ah that explains some of it. if FP16 baseline used 768 then truncation artifacts differ. need identical max_seq across comparisons.

sara: ack. I will re-run baseline with max_seq=512 to keep parity. also will log token offsets to see where truncation clips.

anika: action items: 1) reproduce controlled matrix with consistent max_seq and tokenizer (sara+oli) 2) run 3 seeds + bootstrap 10k for CI (ci-bot) 3) surface per-slice NDCG/MRR and top-10 swap examples in PR (sara) 4) if per-channel PTQ still regresses, test per-layer and alternative calibration (julian).

oli: I'll add a small eval flag `--log-token-boundaries` and a `--stable-tokenizer` mode that pins tokenization artifacts. will open a PR later today.

sara: thanks. quick note: I also saw a tiny improvement on short queries (<=5 tokens) with per-channel PTQ. so it's not uniformly worse.

julian: that's useful — could be shift in pairwise margins. if shorter queries improve and long docs regress, we might tune calibration per sequence-length bucket or use hybrid quant config.

anika: let's record this as a gating check for PTQ rollout: no regression >0.5% absolute MRR on production holdout and p<0.05 continuity required. I'll add to the onboarding checklist.

sara: filing the PR with logs + sample flips + eval matrix once runs complete. link will be posted here.

mike: thanks team. good template for future quant bring-ups — tokenizer parity and seq_len parity first.

ci-bot: queued follow-up runs: matrix (2 tokenizers x 3 quant modes x 3 seeds) estimated runtime 6h. you will be pinged when done.
